scope: The derivation pipeline and index lifecycle: cold-rebuild identity, build_id determinism, structural integrity at index time, and spec index. Belongs here: deleting .spec-engine/ and rebuilding yields an identical result; build_id is deterministic for identical inputs; index-time structural checks; spec index itself. Does not belong here: check severities (CHCK); the SPEC.json envelope shape (SCHM). Boundary case: cold-rebuild identity is INDX's promise even though the model it rebuilds is defined in SCHM.

requirements.statement: Deleting the derived index and rebuilding from the spec location plus repo tags produces an identical result; nothing lives only in the DB.
requirements.why: Canonical truth is the git spec location — the DB is derived and owns nothing.

requirements.statement: Structural integrity (DUP_ID, BROKEN_SUPERSEDE, BAD_STATUS) is validated against the parsed spec at index time, never enforced as DB constraints.
requirements.why: The DB is not the source of truth; constraints there would imply it owns the spec.

requirements.statement: spec index walks the spec location plus member repos and (re)builds the derived SQLite index, reporting build_id and row counts.
requirements.why: Local multi-repo indexing is the substrate every other command reads.

requirements.statement: The tag scanner finds @spec tags anywhere in a line, derives implements/verifies from the file path, and recognizes the optional unit/integration/e2e level token.
requirements.why: Tags are how code claims a requirement; kind-by-path keeps tags one token long.

requirements.statement: The indexer flattens a requirement's cites field into term_citations edges and resolves each citation by TERM id or by exact term name/alias via term_aliases, landing an unresolvable citation with a null term_id.
requirements.why: Requirements should cite canonical glossary terms; resolution reuses the verified relates pipeline (flatten to a derived edge table, resolve names via the aggregate alias map, no FK).

requirements.statement: While a read command serves an existing index that is older than a changed spec file, the command shall warn on stderr that results may be stale and name the --fresh flag.
requirements.why: Editing a spec and then reading old numbers with no signal is how wrong answers get trusted; the warning turns silent staleness into a visible choice.

requirements.statement: When the derived index is deleted and rebuilt from the spec files and member repo tags, the rebuilt index shall be identical to the original, reporting the same build_id for identical inputs.
requirements.why: If any truth lived only in the DB, deleting .spec-engine/ — documented as always safe — would silently lose requirements or coverage, and cold CI rebuilds would disagree with warm local reads.

requirements.statement: If a parsed spec contains a duplicate id, a broken supersede reference, or an invalid status, then spec index shall complete the build and report a DUP_ID, BROKEN_SUPERSEDE, or BAD_STATUS diagnostic instead of rejecting the write.
requirements.why: A structural defect that aborted indexing would blind every read command over one bad entry; a diagnostic keeps the index usable while the defect stays visible where spec check gates it.

requirements.statement: When invoked, spec index shall walk the spec directory and every member repo, rebuild the derived index, and report the build_id and row counts (repos, domains, requirements, tags, diagnostics).
requirements.why: Every other command reads this index; a rebuild that reported nothing would leave no way to confirm what was actually derived, so stale or partial indexes would go unnoticed.

requirements.statement: The tag scanner shall recognize an @spec KEY-NNN tag anywhere in a line regardless of comment style, and shall record the optional trailing level token only when it is unit, integration, or e2e.
requirements.why: Tags are how code claims a requirement; a scanner picky about comment syntax would silently drop claims and understate coverage.

requirements.statement: The scanner shall derive a tag's kind from its file path — a tag in a test file verifies, a tag in any other file implements — and the tag itself never states the kind.
requirements.why: A kind written into the tag would drift from the file's actual role; path derivation keeps tags one token long and impossible to mislabel.

requirements.statement: The indexer shall resolve each requirement citation to a glossary term by TERM id or by exact term name or alias, and shall retain an unresolved citation so spec check can report it as UNDEFINED_TERM.
requirements.why: A citation dropped at resolution time would never surface as a defect — the requirement would silently cite nothing while spec check reported a clean glossary.

requirements.statement: The spec engine shall derive requirements from SPEC.json files only, so a SPEC.md file in a domain directory is never parsed as a spec.
requirements.why: A revived Markdown parse path makes two files compete for the same domain, and the index silently reads whichever one the code found first.

requirements.statement: When walking a member for tags, the scanner shall read .lua, .luau, .go, and .rs files alongside the TypeScript, JavaScript, and shell files, so a requirement implemented in those languages is covered.
requirements.why: A @spec tag in a file the walker never opens is invisible: the requirement it binds reports ORPHAN_REQ or UNVERIFIED_REQ while the code and the test exist.

requirements.statement: When a tag's file ends in _test.go, _test.rs, _spec.lua, or _test.lua, or lives under a spec/ directory, the scanner shall classify the tag as verifies, alongside the .test., .spec., tests/, __tests__/, and e2e paths it already recognizes.
requirements.why: Go, Rust, busted, and the Roblox test runners name test files by their own conventions; a test tag classified as implements leaves the requirement UNVERIFIED_REQ and the coverage matrix wrong for every platform in those languages.

requirements.statement: If any SPEC.json is not JSON or fails the shared schema, then the index build shall refuse to write the index.
requirements.why: A domain dropped from the index turns every reference to it into DANGLING_TAG and BROKEN_RELATES noise that hides the parse error.

requirements.statement: When an index build refuses on an invalid domain file, the spec command that requested it shall print only the INVALID_DOMAIN_FILE rows, naming the file and the failing field, and exit 1.
requirements.why: The root cause has to be the only thing on screen.

requirements.statement: When a member's scan excludes an ignore entry or a sibling workspace package path, the scanner shall match the entry as a repo-relative path prefix.
requirements.why: A module tree that mirrors a package path at depth is never scanned, and its requirements report ORPHAN_REQ while the tags exist.

requirements.statement: When walking a member for tags, the scanner shall read .ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .mjs, .sh, .lua, .luau, .go, .rs, .tf, .toml, .sql, and .css files and any file named Dockerfile or Dockerfile.<suffix>.
requirements.why: A @spec tag in a file the walker never opens is invisible: the requirement it binds reports ORPHAN_REQ or UNVERIFIED_REQ while the code and the test exist.

requirements.statement: When walking a member for tags, the scanner shall read .ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .mjs, .sh, .lua, .luau, .go, .rs, .tf, .toml, .sql, .css, .yml, .yaml, and .astro files and any file named Dockerfile or Dockerfile.<suffix>.
requirements.why: A @spec tag in a file the walker never opens is invisible: the requirement it binds reports ORPHAN_REQ or UNVERIFIED_REQ while the code and the test exist.

requirements.statement: When walking a member for tags, the scanner shall read the .github directory and skip every other dot-prefixed entry.
requirements.why: A CI workflow file is often the only implementation of a promise, and a tag there is invisible while the directory is skipped; opening every dot directory would crawl .venv and tool caches.

requirements.statement: If a domain file holds a duplicate id, a broken supersede, or an invalid status, then spec index shall complete the build and report the matching diagnostic.
requirements.why: A structural defect that aborted indexing would blind every read command over one bad entry; a diagnostic keeps the index usable while the defect stays visible where spec check gates it.

requirements.statement: When spec index runs, it shall report the build_id and the counts of repos, domains, requirements, tags, and diagnostics.
requirements.why: Every other command reads this index; a rebuild that reported nothing would leave no way to confirm what was actually derived, so stale or partial indexes would go unnoticed.

requirements.statement: The tag scanner shall recognize a requirement tag written with any comment leader anywhere in a line.
requirements.why: Tags are how code claims a requirement; a scanner picky about comment syntax would silently drop claims and understate coverage.

requirements.statement: The tag scanner shall classify a tag as verifying when its file path matches a supported test-path pattern, and as implementing otherwise.
requirements.why: A kind written into the tag would drift from the file's actual role; path derivation keeps tags one token long and impossible to mislabel.

requirements.statement: The indexer shall resolve a term citation by TERM id, by headword, or by alias.
requirements.why: A citation dropped at resolution time would never surface as a defect — the requirement would silently cite nothing while spec check reported a clean glossary.

requirements.statement: Where a member config lists ignore directories, the tag scanner shall skip each one as a prefix of the path from the repository root.
requirements.why: A module tree that mirrors a package path at depth is never scanned, and its requirements report ORPHAN_REQ while the tags exist.

requirements.statement: The tag scanner shall record a level token only when it is unit, integration, or e2e.
requirements.why: If any trailing word counted as a level, a typo or a stray word after a tag would show up as a test level in the coverage matrix.

requirements.statement: If a domain directory holds a SPEC.md file, then the spec engine shall derive no requirement from it.
requirements.why: A revived Markdown parse path makes two files compete for the same domain, and the index silently reads whichever one the code found first.

requirements.statement: When an index build refuses on an invalid domain file, the spec command that requested it shall print only the INVALID_DOMAIN_FILE rows, each naming the file and the failing field.
requirements.why: The root cause has to be the only thing on screen.

requirements.statement: When an index build refuses on an invalid domain file, the read or check command that requested it shall exit 1.
requirements.why: CI branches on the exit code, so a refused build that exits 0 passes the gate on an index that was never built.
